Rashi on Arakhin 4a:10:1.hebrew: דמסר להו לצבור וכו' - והלכך, לבן בוכרי דפטר להו לכהנים משקלים, איצטריך מתני' למתני דכהן שהעריך עצמו או את אחר נותן את הערך כישראל, דסד"א כו', קמ"ל (דלא גמירי):
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:10:1.english: That he transfers them to the community, etc. - And therefore, according to ben Bukhri, who exempts priests from [half-]shekels, the Mishnah needed to teach that a priest who valuated himself or another gives the valuation like an Israelite; for it might enter your mind to say, etc. [that since priests are exempt from shekels, they are exempt from valuations], [so the Mishnah] teaches us (that we do not derive [this comparison]).

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:12:1.hebrew: לא יהו פחותין מסלע - דעני בערכין נידון בהשג יד, דכתיב (ויקרא כז): "על פי אשר תשיג יד הנודר וגו'", ופחות מסלע לא יתן לעולם, כדאמר בפ' שני (לקמן ערכין ז:): "אין בערכין פחות מסלע", ומייתי טעמא מהאי קרא. וכיון דלהכי אתא, לא הוה ס"ד למדרש לדרשא אחריתי למפטר כהנים מערכין, ומתני' לא איצטריך:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:12:1.english: [They] shall not be less than a sela - For a poor person in [the case of] valuations is judged according to [his] means, as it is written (Leviticus 27): "According to the means of the vower, etc.," and he shall never give less than a sela, as [the Gemara] says in the second chapter (below, Arakhin 7b): "There is no [valuation] in valuations less than a sela," and it cites the reason from this verse. And since [the verse] came for this [purpose], it would not have entered your mind to expound [it] for another exposition to exempt priests from valuations, and the Mishnah would not have been necessary.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:13:1.hebrew: כהנים נפטרו מפדיון הבן בפ"ק דבכורות (ד.) מק"ו: אם פטרו את של ישראל במדבר, ק"ו את של עצמן:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:13:1.english: Priests were exempted from redemption of the [firstborn] son in the first chapter of Bekhorot (4a) from an a fortiori inference: If they exempted those [firstborn] of Israel in the wilderness, all the more so [they exempt] their own.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:14:1.hebrew: ה"נ דליתנהו באיל אשם - והא ישראל נינהו? אלא ודאי הכי לא דרשי', ואכתי מתני' למה לי למיתני כהנים ולוים וישראלים:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:14:1.english: [Is it] also so that they are not [subject] to a ram of a guilt offering - And [yet] are they not Israelites? Rather, certainly we do not expound thus; and still, why did the Mishnah need to teach "priests, Levites, and Israelites"?

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:15:1.english: And he shall present him before the priest - A poor person who valuated himself or another [person].

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:15:2.hebrew: ולא כהן לפני כהן - הלכך, כהן ליתיה בערכין, דאי עני הוא, לא קרינא ביה "והעמידו לפני הכהן"; קמ"ל מתני':
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:15:2.english: And not a priest before a priest - Therefore, a priest is not [included] in [the laws of] valuations, for if he is poor, we cannot apply to him [the verse], "then he shall be set before the priest"; [therefore,] the Mishnah teaches us [that he is included].

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:16:1.hebrew: נערכין לאתויי כו' - כלומר, אמר מר לעיל: "הכל נערכין — לאתויי מנוול ומוכה שחין":
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:16:1.english: [All] are valuated, to include, etc. - That is to say, the Master stated above [2a]: "All are valuated, to include a disfigured person and one afflicted with boils."

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:17:1.hebrew: ערך סתום - לקמן מפרש, וכולה ברייתא מפרש לקמן:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:17:1.english: An unspecified valuation - [The Gemara] explains [this] below, and the entire Baraita [the Gemara] explains below.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:17:2.hebrew: ערך אבריו - אמר: "ערך ידי עלי" — לא אמר כלום, דאין ערך לאיברים. אבל אם אמר: "דמי ידי עלי" — נותן דמי ידו:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:17:2.english: The valuation of his limbs - [If] one said, "The valuation of my hand is upon me," he has said nothing, for there is no valuation for limbs. But if he said, "The value of my hand is upon me," he gives the value of his hand.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:1:1.hebrew: וגואלין לעולם - אם מכרו שדה, גואלין אותה מיד; וישראל אינו מותר לגאול פחות מב' שנים, כדכתיב: "במספר שני תבואות ימכר לך":
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:1:1.english: And they redeem at any time - If they sold a field, they may redeem it immediately; whereas an Israelite is not permitted to redeem [it in] less than two years, as it is written: "According to the number of years of crops he shall sell to you."

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:1:2.hebrew: נהי דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקעות - כלומר, בכל דין השמטת קרקעות, דהא תנן: מוכרין לעולם:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:1:2.english: Although they are not [subject to] the release of land - That is to say, in all the laws of the release of land, for we learned [in a Mishnah]: "They sell at all times."

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:3:1.hebrew: והך אכילת קדשים משום כפרה הוא, דכתיב: "ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם" — מלמד שהכהנים אוכלין והבעלים מתכפרין (יומא סח:) — אימא: לא תיבעי זימון, קמ"ל כו':
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:3:1.english: And this eating of sacrificial food is for the sake of atonement, as it is written: "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made" — teaching that the priests eat and the owners achieve atonement (Yoma 68b) — [so I might] say: It should not require a zimmun; [therefore] it teaches us, etc.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:5:1.hebrew: מצטרפין כו' - אי אכיל חד כהן וחד לוי וחד ישראל. כהן בהדי זר מצי למיכל מן החולין, הלכך מצטרפין:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:5:1.english: [They] join together, etc. - [This applies] where one priest, one Levite, and one Israelite ate [together]. A priest is able to eat from the non-sacred food along with a non-priest; therefore, they join together.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:7:1.english: [It] is necessary only according to ben Bukhri - At the end of the matter, [the Gemara] explains this [statement] of Rava.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:7:2.english: Who pays - [The] shekels [announced] on the first of Adar.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:7:3.hebrew: אינו חוטא - כדמפרש לקמן, דלא הוו חולין בעזרה, אע"ג דלכתחילה לא מיחייב, דכתיב (שמו' לח): "לכל העובר על הפקודים", ושבט לוי לא נפקד:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:7:3.english: [He] is not a sinner - As [the Gemara] explains below, that they are not non-sacred [items] in the [Temple] courtyard, even though initially he is not obligated, for it is written (Exodus 38): "Everyone that passes among them that are numbered," and the tribe of Levi was not numbered.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:8:1.english: Rather, the priests interpret this verse for themselves - For their own benefit and contrary to the law.

Rashi on Arakhin 4a:9:1.hebrew: שלנו הוא - שהרי מתרומת הלשכה הן באין, ואם אנו שוקלין ללשכה, נמצאת מנחת העומר ושתי הלחם ולחם הפנים משלנו, והיאך נאכלין? הכתיב: "לא תאכל". ולדידן, לית לן הך דרשא, דהאי "כליל תהיה" במנחת כהן גרידתא כתיב, אבל במנחת צבור — זיל בתר רובא:
Rashi on Arakhin 4a:9:1.english: [They] are ours - For they come from the appropriation of the chamber, and if we contribute [shekels] to the chamber, the Omer meal-offering, the Two Loaves, and the Showbread turn out to be [partially] ours, and how can they be eaten? For is it not written: "It shall not be eaten"? And according to us [the Sages], we do not hold this exposition, for this [phrase], "it shall be wholly burnt," is written concerning a priest's meal-offering alone, but concerning a communal meal-offering, follow the majority.

Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:17:1.hebrew: ערך כולו הוא נותן ואינו נותן ערך אברים - דס"ד לרבויי, משום דאדם יודע דאין ערך לאברים, וגמר ואמר לשם כל האברים כולם — קמשמע לן. ועוד י"ל, דסד"א: הואיל [ואיתנהו] אברים (ישנו) בדמים (באברים), איתנהו [נמי] בערכין:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:17:1.english: "He gives the valuation of his entire [self], and he does not give the valuation of limbs" - For one might have thought to include [him to give the full valuation], because a person knows that there is no [statutory] valuation for limbs, and [therefore] he resolved and spoke with intent for all the limbs together [i.e., his entire body]; [the verse therefore] teaches us [that this is not so]. And furthermore, it can be said that one might have thought: Since limbs are subject to [assessment of] monetary value [damim], they should also be subject to [statutory] valuations [arakhin].

Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:1:1.hebrew:
וגואלין לעולם - אם מכרו שדה גואלין אותו מיד, וישראל אינו מותר לגאול פחות מב' שנים, דכתיב (שם): "במספר שני תבואות" וגו'. "נהי דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקע" — כלומר, בכל דין משפט השמטת קרקע, דהא תנן: "ומוכרין לעולם" — ל"ה. ובר"ה (דף כט.) לא גריס רש"י "נהי דליתנהו בהשמטת קרקע", משום דמשמע שאין חוזרת לכהנים ביובל, והא ליתא; ומיהו הכא פי' יפה. וקצת קשה: מה שייכי השמטת קרקע גבי יובל? דהא תניא בספרי: "בשנת היובל הזאת" — זאת מוציאה עבדים (כנענים), ואין השביעית מוציאה עבדים (כנענים). ק"ו ליובל שמשמט: ומה אם השביעית, שאינו מוציא עבדים, משמטת — יובל, שמוציא עבדים, אינו דין שמשמט? ת"ל: "וזה דבר השמטה" — שמטה משמטת, ואין יובל משמט; אלמא אין יובל משמט כספים! ומיהו י"ל: מקצת שייך השמטת כספים גבי יובל, דאין שביעית נוהג אלא בזמן שהיובל נוהג:
והך דאכילת קדשים משום כפרה היא, דכתיב: "ואכלו אותם אשר כופר בהם" וגו', מלמד שהכהנים אוכלים והבעלים מתכפרים, אימא לא תיבעי זימון כו'; "מצטרפין" — אי אכלו חד כהן וחד לוי וחד ישראל, כהן בהדי זר מצי אכיל מן החולין, הלכך מצטרפין — ל"ה. ומכאן נראה, דג' בני אדם המודרים הנאה זה מזה אינן מצטרפין, כיון דאין אחד מהן יכול לאכול עם חבירו. ומיהו נראה, דג' בני אדם המודרין אינה ראיה ברורה, דשאני תרומה, שאין לה היתר לזר אפי' בשאלה, מה שאין במודר הנאה; ובברכות (ד' מה. ד"ה אכל) הארכתי:
Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:1:1.english:
"And they may redeem at any time" - If they sold a field, they may redeem it immediately, whereas an Israelite is not permitted to redeem [a sold ancestral field] in less than two years, as it is written (there, Leviticus 25:15): "According to the number of years of crops [he shall sell to you]" etc. "Although they are not [included] in the release of land" — that is to say, in the entire legal code governing the release of land, for we learned [in a mishna]: "And they may sell at any time" — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And in Rosh HaShana (29a), Rashi did not have the textual reading: "Although they are not [included] in the release of land," because it implies that [land] does not return to the priests in the Jubilee, and that is not so; however, here he explained [it] well. And it is somewhat difficult: What relevance does the release of land [seemingly a scribal error for: cancellation of monetary debts] have to the Jubilee? For it is taught in the Sifrei: "In this year of the Jubilee" (Leviticus 25:13) — this [Jubilee] releases (Canaanite) slaves, but the Sabbatical year does not release (Canaanite) slaves. [One might deduce] an *a fortiori* argument that the Jubilee should release [debts]: If the Sabbatical year, which does not release slaves, releases [debts], is it not logical that the Jubilee, which does release slaves, should release [debts]? [Therefore] the verse states: "And this is the manner of the release" (Deuteronomy 15:2) — the Sabbatical year releases [debts], but the Jubilee does not release [debts]. Evidently, the Jubilee does not cancel monetary debts! However, one can say: The cancellation of monetary debts is somewhat relevant to the Jubilee, for the Sabbatical year applies only when the Jubilee applies.
And that which [Rashi explains: The] consumption of sacrificial foods is for atonement, as it is written: "And they shall eat those things with which atonement was made" etc. (Exodus 29:33), teaching that the priests eat and the owners achieve atonement, [from which one might] say [that] it should not require a *zimmun*, etc.; [and that they] combine [for a *zimmun*]: if one priest, one Levite, and one Israelite ate [together, since] a priest is able to eat non-sacred food [chullin] together with a non-priest [zar], therefore they combine — [this is] the wording of the Kunteres [Rashi]. And from here it would appear that three people who are forbidden by a vow from deriving benefit from one another do not combine [for a *zimmun*], since not one of them is able to eat with his fellow. However, it appears that [the case of] three people who are forbidden by a vow is not a clear proof [from here], for *terumah* is different, as it has no permissibility for a non-priest even through absolution [she'elah], which is not the case for one forbidden by a vow of benefit; and in Berakhot (45a, s.v. Akhal), I have elaborated.

Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:7:1.hebrew: כל כהן שאינו שוקל חוטא - דדריש "זה יתנו" — י"ב שבטים בגימטריא ז"ה. וה"נ מצי למימר: "כל לוי שאינו שוקל", אלא משום דלא מצי למימר: "משום שדורשין מקרא זה לעצמן":
Tosafot on Arakhin 4a:7:1.english: "Any priest who does not contribute [the half-shekel] is a sinner" - For he expounds "This [zeh] they shall give" [as referring to] twelve tribes, according to the numerical value [gematria] of zeh [ז"ה = 12]. And he could also have said: "Any Levite who does not contribute [the half-shekel] [is a sinner]"; rather, [he formulated it regarding priests] because [regarding a Levite] he could not have said: "Because they expound this verse to their own [advantage]."
